city.Djibouti.description: This small, super-hot country on the Horn of Africa sits beside the Red Sea. It is famous for blinding-white salt lakes, spooky limestone chimneys, and gentle whale sharks that gather in its warm gulf.
city.Djibouti.landmark: blinding white salt shores and turquoise water of Lake Assal
city.Djibouti.greeting: People speak Arabic and French — in Arabic, hello is “Marhaba” (mar-HA-ba).

city.Equatorial Guinea.description: This small Central African country is split between a jungle mainland and islands out in the Gulf of Guinea. It is the only African nation where Spanish is the main language, a leftover from long-ago Spanish rule.
city.Equatorial Guinea.landmark: volcanic peak of Pico Basile rising over the rainforest and coast of Bioko Island
city.Equatorial Guinea.greeting: Spanish is spoken here — say hello with “Hola” (OH-la).

city.Eritrea.description: This country on the Red Sea coast of the Horn of Africa mixes scorching desert lowlands with a cool mountain capital, Asmara, where old Italian-style cafés still serve espresso from colonial days.

city.Ethiopia.description: This mountainous country in the Horn of Africa is often called the birthplace of coffee. It keeps its own calendar and clock, and is famous for churches carved downward out of solid rock at Lalibela.
city.Ethiopia.landmark: cross-shaped rock-hewn church of Bete Giyorgis carved down into the stone at Lalibela
